text: Five accounts say buy. Is that five opinions? Or one opinion, copied four times?
Most trading bots can't tell the difference. They count the noise, act on it, and keep no record of why.
This is Hanko. A hanko is the seal you stamp in Japan to commit to something. Every decision here is stamped before the outcome is known.
It reads public voices on Telegram, Bluesky and X. A repost, a forward, or a copy with an ad pasted on counts as one voice. Not two.
Then it decides. Enter, pass, or admit it can't tell. It sizes the position, and writes down in advance exactly what would prove it wrong.
Every run is sealed and anchored in a Bitcoin block. Change one byte, and the seal breaks. Anyone can check it, with no account and no key.
Before it buys, it checks it can sell. Selling fifty thousand dollars of BONK costs under three percent, from a real quote. The textbook formula said seven point six.
So we broke it on purpose. Sources down. Rate limits. A planted instruction. Tampered evidence. Nine failures. Nine held.
And it runs every three hours, on its own, in public. Three days later, every call is graded against the conditions it set itself.
Hanko. Don't trust the call. Check the receipt.
